Nodes validate identities by solving hardware-bound puzzles that scale with local ambient temperature, treating sustained heat emission as the scarce resource. To register a fake node, an attacker must acquire and power dedicated thermal generators, burning real timber for physical baseline calibration. This infrastructure forces a thermodynamic anchor: every identity demands continuous, unreclaimable energy dissipation, turning any systemic scale attempt into a fable of diminishing economic returns.
